title: 1956 AHSME Problem 29
statement: The points of intersection of \(xy=12\) and \(x^2+y^2=25\) are joined in succession. The resulting figure is:

solutions.text:
At an intersection, \[ \begin{aligned} (x+y)^2&=x^2+y^2+2xy\\ &=25+24=49, \end{aligned} \] so \(x+y=\pm7.\) Together with \(xy=12,\) this gives the four points \[ \begin{aligned} &(3,4),\ (4,3),\\ &(-3,-4),\ (-4,-3). \end{aligned} \] In their cyclic order around the circle, adjacent side vectors are perpendicular, so the quadrilateral is a rectangle. Its adjacent side lengths are unequal, so it is not a square.

Thus, the correct answer is D.
hints: Use \((x+y)^2=x^2+y^2+2xy\) to find the possible sums \(x+y\)
The four intersection points are permutations and negatives of \((3,4)\)
